messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool 'primary-eu1' queue growth >95% over 5m. Autoscaler attempted scaleup but received quota_exceeded from cloud provider. Throttling incoming requests. Pager: oncall-sre.

alice (oncall): ack. looking at dashboards (latency, queue_length, autoscaler events). tagging eng/sre.

alice (oncall): autoscaler log excerpt: 
```
scaleup: requested=6 gpus
scaleup: rejected reason=quota_exceeded code=403 provider=cloud-eu1
```
Nodes stuck in Provisioning state.

bob (sre): I see many pods in Pending -> ContainerCreating. Cloud console shows insufficient GPUs in zone. Looks like region-level capacity exhaustion. Also seeing increased OOMs on a few pods causing restart loops.

carla (runtime): traffic is partially spilling to eu2 butSticky routing keys keep some sessions pinned to eu1. Control-plane is not performing a full failover because circuit-breaker thresholds were not tripped. Result: eu1 still receives a significant portion and is overloaded.

dan (eng-ml): heads up: fallback to smaller model variants is configured but strict compatibility checks are blocking some sessions (v2-large clients expect v2-large). If we allow permissive fallback we'll reduce GPU pressure but risk degradation in output quality.

alice (oncall): runbook step: try graceful cross-region evacuation. Doing routing adjustment: `/route adjust --from=eu1 --to=eu2 --weight=0.6 --reason="evac primary-eu1 due to capacity"`

incident-bot: action logged: routing change executed by alice (oncall). previous_weights={eu1:0.85,eu2:0.15} new_weights={eu1:0.4,eu2:0.6}.

carla (runtime): control-plane reports eu1 ~40% traffic, eu2 ~60%. However sticky-session cookies (X-Client-Session) still direct ~18% traffic to eu1. Recommend enabling header-based reroute to break stickiness for new requests: `/route force-reroute --header=X-Client-Session`

bob (sre): requesting emergency reserved capacity in eu1: bump dedicated-pool primary-eu1 from 10->16 GPUs. Cloud account shows soft quota, needs infra approval. If approved we'll provision and then gradually move traffic back.

eve (support): pinging top impacted customers. They're reporting 503s and long tails on completions. Notifying them of mitigation actions: routing change + trying quota bump. Estimated ETA 20-30m to stabilize.

alice (oncall): blocked on quota approval. Paging infra: @frank (infra) can you expedite gpu quota bump for eu1 (+6 for 1h)?

frank (infra): acknowledged. submitting quota increase request to cloud provider console and raising with on-call ops. ETA ~7m for approval, then provisioning time ~6-12m depending on placement.

dan (eng-ml): temporary action: recommend enabling quantized fallback variant v2-large -> v2-medium-quant for non-enterprise clients to reduce per-session GPU memory and allow more concurrency. Command: `/models set-fallback --model=v2-large --fallback=v2-medium-quant --rate=0.25`

carla (runtime): applied permissive fallback policy at 25% traffic and turned on KV-cache sharing across compatible variants. Also enabled auto-retry to non-sticky routing for failed sticky sessions. These changes should reduce instantaneous GPU footprint.

alice (oncall): autoscaler events - new attempts show fewer rejections after quota approval kicked off. queue_length in eu1 trending downward now that traffic shifted to eu2. Monitoring closely.

bob (sre): quota approved by infra; cloud account allocated +6 GPUs. Provisioning in progress; 4/6 nodes are ready, 2 still pending due to placement-group constraints. Health checks passing on ready nodes.

eve (support): customers acknowledging the update. One large enterprise asked to keep all their traffic routed to eu2 until we confirm eu1 health — set per-customer routing override for customer-id=ACME.

alice (oncall): decision: keep split routing (eu1=~40% eu2=~60%) and permissive fallbacks until all new nodes are ready and eu1 tail latency sits below 200ms for 10 minutes. Creating incident channel #inc-2723456789 for detailed coordination and postmortem. Severity: SEV2.

dan (eng-ml): note for postmortem: add flag in deployment to allow controlled degradation (quality vs availability) via Console toggle; avoid manual CLI toggles in future.

alice (oncall): created postmortem checklist and initial timeline. tagging owners: eng-runtime, eng-ml, infra, support. Will do a 1hr follow-up. Leaving monitoring alerts open; closing immediate page but will re-page if queue growth resumes.

incident-bot: monitoring continues. Alert state: mitigated (routing change + quota bump + fallbacks). Will escalate if queue >70% again for 5m.

alice (oncall): final note: follow-up action items recorded: 1) Console feature for permissive fallback toggles, 2) improve automatic circuit-breaker failover thresholds, 3) document per-customer override flow. End of thread.
